title: Transport canonical neighbourhood geometry to the small colimit model
statement: Let f:X→S be any scheme morphism and s:Spec Ω→S a geometric point, with Ω algebraically closed. The canonical comparison Spec(smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso(s).inv) induces an isomorphism from X×_S strictHenselizationScheme(s) to X×_S strictLocalization(s). For every canonical StrictLocalNeighbourhoodGeometry Q of [def-weil-pbc-strict-local-neighbourhood-geometry], precomposing its legs with this isomorphism produces a limiting cone on the identical small affine-neighbourhood pullback diagram. The transported legs have projection to X equal to pullback.fst and first component equal to pullback.snd followed by the original small-model strictHenselizationCone leg and Spec(ΓSpecIso.inv). No qcqs hypothesis is needed for this transport.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, theorem-higher-direct-images, first proof paragraph (fibre products commute with the affine-neighbourhood limit); smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso and its inverse coprojection formula. Canonical-model compatibility proof by T6.

proof.text: Use the structural-map identity supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-small-closed-fiber-comparison] to form pullback.map with identity on X and S and Spec of the inverse canonical colimit comparison on the strict-local scheme. All three component maps are isomorphisms, so Mathlib pullback.map_isIso gives the comparison isomorphism.

Extend the canonical geometry cone by the comparison hom. Cone.extendIso and IsLimit.ofIsoLimit give its limiting property. Compose the upstream over equation with the comparison; the pullback first projection equation proves the transported over equation.

Apply Functor.Final.ι_colimitIso_inv to the representative functor followed by the affine pointed-neighbourhood inclusion. Applying Spec identifies Spec(c.inv) followed by each canonical cone leg with the original small-model cone leg. Compose the upstream first equation with the pullback comparison and use pullback.lift_snd_assoc and this leg identity. This proves the first-component equation exactly, including the specified Gamma-Spec inverse.

theorem smallModelFirst {X S : Scheme.{v}} {f : X ⟶ S}
    {Ω : Type v} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] {s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S}
    (Q : StrictLocalNeighbourhoodGeometry f s)
    (i : SmallModel.{v} (Scheme.strictHenselizationNeighbourhoods s)) :
    Q.smallModelLegs.app i ≫ pullback.fst ((strictLocalNeighbourhoods s).obj i).hom f =
      pullback.snd f (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap s) ≫
        (Scheme.strictHenselizationCone s).π.app (op (op i)) ≫
          Spec.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso
            ((equivSmallModel.{v} (Scheme.strictHenselizationNeighbourhoods s)).inverse.obj
              i).1.left.unop).inv
